title: Design System: Trash Dash: Alley Acres

display.purpose: Game title and decisive state headings.

label.purpose: Uppercase status categories and compact controls.

shadows.name: cabinet-lift
shadows.purpose: Separates the playable stage from the deep teal field.

shadows.name: hud-lift
shadows.purpose: Keeps live game status legible over the cabinet.

shadows.name: control-lift
shadows.purpose: Makes compact actions tactile without hard offset styling.

motion.name: control-ease
motion.purpose: Hover, press, and focus response on controls.

motion.name: camera-follow
motion.purpose: Smooth horizontal tracking with the raccoon held left of center.

components.name: Primary Action
components.description: The strongest state-changing action, rendered in Momentum Orange.
components.css: .ds-primary { min-height: 48px; padding: 0 20px; border: 0; border-radius: 13px; background: #f28b2d; color: #172a2b; font: 1000 16px 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 5px 12px rgb(1 22 24 / 26%); transition: transform 140ms ease-out, background-color 140ms ease-out, box-shadow 140ms ease-out; } .ds-primary:hover { background: #ffab42; transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 7px 16px rgb(1 22 24 / 32%); } .ds-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffe174; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: HUD Utility
components.description: Short pause and sound controls that remain available during play.
components.css: .ds-utility { min-width: 42px; min-height: 38px; padding: 0 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 11px; background: #087c86; color: #fff4ce; font: 1000 12px 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 5px 12px rgb(1 22 24 / 26%); transition: transform 140ms ease-out, background-color 140ms ease-out; } .ds-utility:hover { background: #0a929d; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-utility:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffe174; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: HUD Status
components.description: A compact label/value pair for trash, score, time, paws, and glider state.
components.css: .ds-status { display: grid; gap: 1px; color: #fff4ce; font-family: 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; } .ds-status span { color: #b9ddcc; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 900; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-status strong { font-size: 16px; line-height: 1; }

components.name: Pocket Jump
components.description: The dominant right-thumb control in portrait play.
components.css: .ds-jump { width: 54px; height: 54px; border: 0; border-radius: 12px; background: rgb(242 139 45 / 92%); color: #3c2919; font: 1000 12px 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 5px 12px rgb(1 22 24 / 26%); touch-action: none; } .ds-jump:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(.98); } .ds-jump:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffe174; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Game Stage
components.description: The crisp 16:9 playable surface and visual authority for the product.
components.css: .ds-stage { display: grid; place-items: center; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 16px; background: #73d8f4; color: #163c3c; font: 900 12px 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 24px 60px rgb(0 8 8 / 45%); image-rendering: pixelated; }

narrative.overview: Trash Dash should feel like a complete late-16-bit game world held directly in the browser. The interface recedes behind the playable artifact: a compact equipment-like HUD and a large pixel stage, with the supplied raccoon artwork providing personality and visual authority.
keyCharacteristics: The playable pixel world owns the viewport.
Teal utility surfaces frame sky, leaf, dirt, and orange action color.
Controls are chunky, short-labeled, and thumb-friendly.
Animation is purposeful and tied to gameplay state.
Desktop uses a 16:9 cabinet; portrait play adds a dedicated pocket-control deck.

rules.name: Orange Means Go
rules.body: Reserve orange for titles, the strongest action, pickups, and celebratory state; it should not become general decoration.

rules.name: Cartridge Voice
rules.body: Use the display face for identity and decisive state changes, never for paragraphs or dense instruction.

dos: Do let the supplied sprite artwork lead every playable screen.
Do keep physics bodies slightly forgiving while anchoring visible sprites to a shared baseline.
Do keep portrait controls outside the 16:9 playfield.
donts: Don't wrap the game in generic website navigation, marketing sections, or equal-sized cards.
Don't stretch, smooth, or blur pixel assets.
Don't obscure the stage with touch controls.
